title: Overview
summary: A quick introduction to the TDS Benchmark platform.

content.text: TDS Benchmark helps researchers and practitioners evaluate tabular data synthesis tools with a consistent and reproducible process.
You can compare tools across privacy, utility, robustness, and computational performance dimensions.
Each section in this documentation is configured from JSON blocks, so adding richer content does not require component rewrites.

content.caption: High-level benchmark flow used for evaluation and decision support.

title: Getting Started
summary: How to begin using the benchmark in a few steps.

content.text: Start from the Synthesis page and answer questions about your dataset structure, temporal dependencies, and privacy requirements.

items: Upload and inspect your real tabular dataset.
Select synthesis goals (augmentation, balancing, or robust generation).
Choose evaluation priorities and compute constraints.
Review recommended tools and run benchmark outputs.

content.caption: Main flow for end-users starts from the synthesis assistant.

title: Input Requirements
summary: What data and metadata should be prepared before benchmarking.

content.text: Prepare your source data as clean tabular files with consistent schema and encoded missing values.

items: Feature typing: numerical, categorical, binary, and temporal columns.
Target constraints: privacy budget, class imbalance objectives, and utility goals.
Runtime context: CPU or GPU availability, memory ceiling, and expected turnaround time.

content.text: Inconsistent column typing between train and validation splits can invalidate metric comparisons.

title: Evaluation Metrics
summary: Understand each quality dimension used in the benchmark.

content.text: Metrics are grouped to show distribution alignment, relationship preservation, predictive utility, and privacy risk.

items: Marginal Distribution: fidelity of feature-level distributions.
Dependency Structure: preservation of inter-column relationships.
Utility: downstream model performance with synthetic data.
Privacy and Robustness: leakage risk and stability under stress conditions.

title: FAQ
summary: Common questions from users and researchers.

items: Q: Can I benchmark a custom synthesis model? A: Yes, align outputs to the framework's expected interface.
Q: Do I need a GPU? A: Not always. Many tools run on CPU with longer training times.
Q: Which metric is most important? A: Prioritize based on your objective (privacy or ML utility).
